Purely luck-based game, with no room for skill or strategy to influence the outcome. Even if you consistently make statistically optimal choices, you might still end up losing and having to go through the same frustrating s**t all over again. Only bought the game because of the price and seemingly small number of achievements. However, getting a Platinum for this game would take a lot of unnecessary time because it turns out you are required to collect all of the tapes. That would be fine if the gameplay had more to offer but it offers nothing rewarding or engaging beyond its basic mechanics which are getting stale extremely fast. Do not recommend.

The first few runs are effectively tense with the visuals and atmospehere to seal the deal, which would have made for an easy recomend (espescialy considering the asking price) had that inital impression lasted. Repeat playthorughs to get to the ending disolves all tension once you've figured how to win, making the game a monotonous grind: Once the horror aesthetics have washed over you, the game is as compelling as data entry. The game's gambling mechanics are lackluster, and not advantageous for the player to utalize. Unlockable tapes, which can be unlocked from the menu anyway, and the ending are not worth the twenty or so times you need to complete the game to see them.
Visuals and aesthetics are the strengths of this game. It gets a bit repetitive after a while, but it has a lot of quality to offer for only 2 euros. The ending was special.

EN: This is Dota, stripped of graphics, heroes, and lore. It's the naked 'Double or Nothing' mechanic, where instead of a 'Higher/Lower' button, you press 'Find Match'.
